style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, top-down 90-degree view, 50mm lens, crisp plane focus, fine film grain. Split-screen diptych on a warm oak home-office desk: left third, one slim bone-white mailbox bill, blank paper with cropped illegible header, a payment card tucked beneath; right two-thirds, a thick fanned stack of graphite-grey ruled maintenance log sheets, one sheet creased and out of alignment, a steel wristwatch resting on top. A slim brushed-steel ruler laid vertically forms the clean seam between halves. Soft diffused daylight from the left, muted paper tones of bone white, graphite and warm oak, generous negative space, no people, no legible text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, legible numbers, watermarks
rationale: The story turns on two published numbers — a $60 fee and a $47.66 wage — which is exactly the treatment's trigger: a rate notice that changed the economics. A top-down flat-lay is the site's own world of household money and paperwork, and the split-screen duality states the build-vs-buy trade physically: one small visible sheet against a large sprawl of invisible hours.
cue: trades a small visible bill for a large invisible one
subject: a slim mailbox bill beside a thick stack of maintenance log sheets on a desk
core_thesis: Self-hosting swaps a small bill you can see for a bigger one you cannot: at the 2025 median admin wage of $47.66 an hour, just 1.26 hours of upkeep a year erases the $60 saved on a managed mailbox.
core_conflict: The small, published, visible cash fee of managed services versus the large, invisible, unpaid labor cost of maintaining your own stack — two public numbers and one division that settles the money question.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast, the seam an off-centre vertical steel ruler

review.depicts: A slim white envelope with a dark bank card tucked under it on the left of a wooden desk, a vertical steel ruler standing at the centre seam, and a thick stack of white log-style sheets with a silver wristwatch lying on top at the right.
review.reason: The frame literally stages the article's mechanism — a thin bill versus a thick stack of maintenance records — with the watch and ruler reinforcing the hours-versus-dollars break-even, so a reader would recognize the story despite no legible text.
